\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أنتج} (antaja)}{أنتج (antaja)}]{\ar{أنتج} (antaja) — to produce}

\label{lesson:AR-C525-antaja}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to be promoted, then the Arabic for headquarters.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أنتج}}
\textbf{\ar{أنتج}} — \emph{antaja} — \textquotedblleft{}to produce\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ينتج} \ar{المصنع} \ar{ألف} \ar{سيارة} \ar{كل} \ar{شهر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yuntiju al-maṣnaʿ alf sayyāra kull shahr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The factory produces a thousand cars every month.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينتج}, \emph{yuntij}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أنتج}} (\emph{antaja}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-t-j}, \textquotedblleft{}to bring forth young\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Natīja, a result, which you know, is from the same root: what a thing brings forth.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{antaja}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{antaja}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yuntiju al-maṣnaʿ alf sayyāra kull shahr.} — The factory produces a thousand cars every month.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to be promoted, then the Arabic for headquarters, then say \emph{antaja} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أنتج} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To produce\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صمم} (ṣammama)}{صمم (ṣammama)}]{\ar{صمم} (ṣammama) — to design}

\label{lesson:AR-C525-sammama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for headquarters, then the Arabic for to produce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صمم}}
\textbf{\ar{صمم}} — \emph{ṣammama} — \textquotedblleft{}to design\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{صممت} \ar{أختي} \ar{فستان} \ar{العروس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṣammamat ukhtī fustān al-ʿarūs.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister designed the bride's dress.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يصمم}, \emph{yuṣammim}.

With \ar{على} it means to be determined: \ar{صمم} \ar{على} \ar{السفر}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صمم}} (\emph{ṣammama}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-m-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to be solid, closed up\textquotedblright{}. Its older sense is to be firmly resolved; the sense of designing is modern.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣammama}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣammama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣammamat ukhtī fustān al-ʿarūs.} — My sister designed the bride's dress.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for headquarters, then the Arabic for to produce, then say \emph{ṣammama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{صمم} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To design\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مصمم} (muṣammim)}{مصمم (muṣammim)}]{\ar{مصمم} (muṣammim) — a designer}

\label{lesson:AR-C525-musammim}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to produce, then the Arabic for to design.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مصمم}}
\textbf{\ar{مصمم}} — \emph{muṣammim} — \textquotedblleft{}a designer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يعمل} \ar{ابن} \ar{خالتي} \ar{مصمما} \ar{في} \ar{شركة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yaʿmalu ibn khālatī muṣammiman fī sharika.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My cousin works as a designer in a company.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مصمم}} (\emph{muṣammim}) is the participle of Form II \emph{ṣammama}, \textquotedblleft{}to design\textquotedblright{}, which is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-m-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to be solid\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muṣammim}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yaʿmalu ibn khālatī muṣammiman fī sharika.} — My cousin works as a designer in a company.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to produce, then the Arabic for to design, then say \emph{muṣammim} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{برمج} (barmaja)}{برمج (barmaja)}]{\ar{برمج} (barmaja) — to program (a computer)}

\label{lesson:AR-C525-barmaja}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to design, then the Arabic for a designer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{برمج}}
\textbf{\ar{برمج}} — \emph{barmaja} — \textquotedblleft{}to program (a computer)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{برمج} \ar{أخي} \ar{لعبة} \ar{على} \ar{الحاسوب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{barmaja akhī luʿba ʿalā al-ḥāsūb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother programmed a game on the computer.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يبرمج}, \emph{yubarmij}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{برمج}} (\emph{barmaja}) is a modern Arabic verb built from \emph{barnāmaj}, \textquotedblleft{}a programme\textquotedblright{}, which you know; \emph{barnāmaj} is usually traced to Persian \emph{barnāma}. Arabic made a new four-letter root \emph{b-r-m-j} from it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barmaja}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barmaja}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barmaja akhī luʿba ʿalā al-ḥāsūb.} — My brother programmed a game on the computer.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to design, then the Arabic for a designer, then say \emph{barmaja} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{برمج} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To program (a computer)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مبرمج} (mubarmij)}{مبرمج (mubarmij)}]{\ar{مبرمج} (mubarmij) — a programmer}

\label{lesson:AR-C525-mubarmij}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a designer, then the Arabic for to program.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مبرمج}}
\textbf{\ar{مبرمج}} — \emph{mubarmij} — \textquotedblleft{}a programmer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
